html:
The Ngarla are an Aboriginal people of the Pilbara coast in Western Australia, around the De Grey River east of present day Port Hedland.

Their neighbours were the Kariyarra to the west, the Nyamal inland and the Nyangumarta along the coast to the northeast. The De Grey was one of the first areas in the northwest taken up for sheep in the 1860s, and Ngarla people were drawn into station work and pearling. The language has very few speakers today. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Ngarla are an Aboriginal people of the Pilbara coast in Western Australia, around the De Grey River east of present day Port Hedland.
